mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes G Class G 65 AMG engine in the UK?

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M279 turbocharger failure in a G 65 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M279's twin-turbo system has several warning signs before complete failure. Loss of power or reduced boost pressure. Excessive smoke from the exhaust. Loud whining noise from the engine bay. Check engine light illuminated. Fault codes related to turbocharger performance.

mainEntity.name: Is the M279 V12 engine in the G 65 AMG reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M279 V12 is a masterpiece of engineering but requires meticulous maintenance. It is generally reliable when properly maintained, but has several well-documented issues. Turbocharger failure due to heat and oil contamination. Intercooler leaks causing reduced boost pressure. Ignition coil failures due to heat exposure. Oil leaks from degraded seals and gaskets. Regular maintenance with correct 0W-40 oil and 5,000-7,000 mile intervals is critical.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my G 65 AMG engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., turbo seals, ignition coils, intercooler). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic turbo failure that has sent debris through the engine. Turbo seal/actuator repair: £1,500-£2,500 - excellent value if caught early. Intercooler replacement: £2,000-£3,000 - essential maintenance. Ignition coil set replacement: £900-£1,500 - preventative if caught early. Full M279 V12 rebuild: £15,000-£25,000 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given G 65 AMG values (£80,000-£150,000+), a rebuilt engine is excellent value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my G 65 AMG has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. G 65 AMG (2012-2018): M279.982 (6.0L V12 twin-turbo). Service history documents list engine type.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG relies on the M279 V12 twin-turbo - an engine of extraordinary complexity and capability. While fundamentally robust when properly maintained, the V12's intricate systems have developed well-documented reputations for specific, expensive failures. Turbocharger failure, intercooler leaks, ignition coil degradation, and oil leaks dominate replacement demand. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common G 65 AMG engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M279 Turbocharger Failure - Why the G 65 AMG Loses Power and Generates Smoke
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG (M279.982, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: The twin-turbocharged V12 generates immense heat, which can cause oil seals to degrade and turbocharger bearings to wear prematurely. Excessive heat, oil contamination, or worn-out seals cause the turbos to fail. When this happens, owners may notice a loss of power, excessive smoke from the exhaust, or a loud whining noise from the engine bay. Vacuum lines and wastegate actuators also tend to wear out over time, affecting turbo performance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbo seals, wastegate actuators, inspect turbo cores
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-70k miles; viable if turbo cores are healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both turbochargers, new oil lines, gaskets, heat shields
repairOptions.longevity: 70k-100k miles; if turbo failure is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M279 V12 with upgraded turbos, new seals
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic turbo debris ingestion

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 65 AMG is worth £80,000-£150,000+ depending on condition and mileage. The full replacement cost of £15,000-£25,000 is small relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine excellent value for preservation. For vehicles worth under £60,000 (high-mileage examples), evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: On a G 65 AMG worth £80,000-£150,000+, specialist turbocharger repair at £1,500-£2,500 is the obvious first step if caught early. Dealer pricing is significantly inflated for this repair. However, if the failure has caused turbo debris to enter the engine (metal particles in oil), you must go straight to full engine replacement - ignoring this risks complete bottom end failure within 1,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M279 Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: M279 Intercooler & Cooling System Failures - Why the G 65 AMG Loses Boost and Overheats
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG (M279.982, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: The G 65 AMG produces immense power, generating excessive heat that places the cooling system under constant stress. Intercooler leaks reduce the efficiency of the turbo system, causing reduced boost pressure, sluggish acceleration, and increased fuel consumption. Radiator leaks (the radiator is made with a mix of aluminium and plastic that degrades over time) and water pump failure are also common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace thermostat, inspect hoses, pressure test system
Replace both intercoolers, new coolant, system bleed, pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-80k miles; essential if boost pressure is reduced

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace radiator, water pump, coolant hoses, full system flush
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles; if coolant leaks are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M279 V12 with new cooling system components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if overheating has caused damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 65 AMG worth £80,000-£150,000+, the intercooler replacement at £2,000-£3,000 is essential maintenance. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The cooling system on the M279 V12 is critical to engine longevity. If you notice reduced boost pressure, sluggish acceleration, or coolant loss, have the intercoolers and cooling system inspected immediately. Specialist replacement is significantly cheaper than dealer pricing and far less expensive than a full engine rebuild. Don't ignore coolant loss - overheating a V12 can cause catastrophic engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M279 Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG engine prices

problems.group: M279 Ignition Coil & Oil Leak Problems
problems.h4: M279 Ignition Coil & Oil Leak Problems - Why the G 65 AMG Misfires and Drips Oil
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 65 AMG (M279.982, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: The V12's ignition coils are exposed to significant heat from the engine and can fail, leading to misfires, poor fuel consumption, and a lack of power. Oil leaks from degraded seals and gaskets are also common on higher-mileage V12 engines. Carbon buildup in the intake system due to direct fuel injection causes rough idling, power loss, and misfires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 12 ignition coils, spark plugs, inspect wiring
Walnut blast intake valves, clean throttle body, reset adaptations
Replace valve cover gaskets, oil cooler seals, camshaft seals
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles; if multiple oil leaks present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M279 V12 with new ignition components, seals
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 65 AMG worth £80,000-£150,000+, ignition coil replacement at £900-£1,500 is sensible maintenance. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The M279 V12's ignition coils are a known weak point due to heat exposure. Replacing all 12 coils as a preventative measure at 60,000 miles is recommended - doing individual coils as they fail leads to repeated workshop visits and potential engine damage from misfires. For oil leaks, address them early; V12 oil leaks can quickly become expensive if left unchecked.
